chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhur, from his father, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Uthman ibn Rushayd, from Ma'ruf ibn Kharbouz, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, paired the Zakat with the Salat, so He said: 'Establish the Salat and give the Zakat.'
Thus, the one who establishes the Salat and does not give the Zakat has not established the Salat.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between Salat and Zakat in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) elucidates that the Quranic coupling of Zakat with Salat signifies their intrinsic unity, where neglecting one invalidates the spiritual integrity of the other. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that Zakat is not merely a supplementary charity but an essential component of 'establishing' prayer, reflecting the holistic nature of worship in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Usman Bin Rusheyd, from Marouf bin Kharbouz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Paired the Zakāt with the Salāt, so Heazwj Said [2:43] And establish the Salāt and give the Zakāt.
Thus, the one who establishes the Salāt and does not give the Zakāt has not established the Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 23. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Jumhur from his father from Ali ibn Hadid from ‘Uthman from ibn Rashid from Ma‘ruf ibn Kharrabuz who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has joined zakat with Salah (prayer), saying, “Maintain Salah (prayer) and pay zakat.”
Thus, if one does not pay zakat, he has not performed Salah (prayer).”’
